newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO steady to firm amid Iraq tensions.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO steady to firm amid Iraq tensions.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were expected to edge higher amid renewed US/Iraq tensions, but healthy supplies may offset the gain, traders said.
Singapore residue stocks in the week ended September 11, rose sharply by over 1.04 million barrels to 9.86 million barrels.
In the swaps market, September was quoted bid/asked at $114.50/$115.50 against $114/$115 per tonne.
Traders said prices were likely to move higher with the renewed US/Iraq tension, tracking crude gains.

IPE October Brent crude futures touched a five-year high to hit $23.82 after Iraq said it would resist U.S military action and its imposition of no-fly zones. Levels later eased to $23.74 by late Thursday.

Traders said at least two majors, two Singapore traders and a Dutch trader still have October cargoes. South Korean supplies in October were limited to two to three cargoes. These cargoes were expected to move into China, traders said.
Traders said the Japanese trader who purchased 40,000 tonnes of fuel oil on Wednesday, was shortcovering for its requirement in China.
Bunker demand were thin, providing little support to cargo prices, traders said. -- Singapore newsroom (65-870-3082)
